additions.site_identity_review: The notice places 26/03028/REM on 'Phase 2 of the data centre campus' at the 'Land at Former Power Station Site on Northern Side of Cambois' and makes it pursuant to outline permission 24/04112/OUTES. The Environment Agency-hosted QTS Project Wind Environmental Setting and Site Design Report (Cundall, November 2025; the evidence behind this site's existing campus locator) states that QTS Data Centres is developing the Cambois Campus on the former coal-stock yards of Blyth Power Station and that 24/04112/OUTES is the outline permission for the entire Cambois Campus site (up to ten data centre buildings, up to 540,000 m2 GIA), granted on 8 May 2025, with enabling works approved under 25/01725/REM. The 9 October 2026 council notice ties the same outline reference and the same applicant, Renaissance Land Limited (recorded in the Atlas source record as the Blackstone-owned entity financing the QTS project), to the former power station site at NE22 7BL, the postcode of the Environment Agency permit application for QTS Project Wind (Rainton Construction Limited, EPR/JP3321LF/A001). Phase 2 is therefore a further phase of the existing QTS Cambois campus, not a new site; it is distinct from the existing campus-wide record and from the 2026 earthworks record, and from Phase A (the first two data centre units).

status.summary: Northumberland County Council's statutory notice dated 25 September 2026 publicises reserved matters application 26/03028/REM by Renaissance Land Limited for appearance, landscaping, layout and scale of two data centre buildings with ancillary offices (Use Class B8) and associated landscaping and infrastructure on Phase 2 of the Cambois data centre campus, pursuant to outline permission 24/04112/OUTES. This dated government record identifies the Phase 2 project, so it is announced as of 25 September 2026. The reserved matters are undecided in the notice, so permitted status is not asserted for Phase 2 (the 2025 outline consent alone leaves its detailed design unapproved and predates the window), and no works on Phase 2 are implied.

additions.successor_review: The notice invites representations within 21 days of 25 September 2026 and records no decision. Northumberland's planning portal (publicaccess.northumberland.gov.uk) disallows all agents in robots.txt and was not read, so a decision issued in October 2026 cannot be excluded; it would be a later, separate observation. The council's 9 October 2026 notice (26/02919/FUL, temporary 60kV substation for construction and early operation of the campus) and the 4 September 2026 notice (26/02818/FUL, 11/33kV temporary substations) concern grid infrastructure and do not report Phase 2 works. QTS's news sitemap (re-read 23 October 2026) lists no Cambois item other than the October 2025 social-value release. Phase 2 stays announced as of 25 September 2026.

The 4 September 2026 notice is by the same applicant for the same named campus, on land east of Sleekburn Business Centre, West Sleekburn, an address separate from the former power station site (whether it lies within the outline application boundary was not established).

This dated landowner disclosure shows the Microsoft data-centre development at Skelton Grange to be a live, named project on 19 August 2026. status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the existing 27 April 2026 observation. Harworth's half-year results announcement of 9 September 2026 (local harworth-hy2026-results-20260909.html, sha256 64463acd...) repeats that the final plot sale to Microsoft at Skelton Grange is progressing towards completion; it is not used as the observation because it is a period report (six months to 30 June 2026), following the thirty-first holds' treatment of that RNS. Harworth's post list re-read on 23 October 2026 (local harworth-wp-posts-20261023.json) has nothing after 18 September 2026 (a St Helens land sale); no completion of the Microsoft plot sale, decision notice or start of works at Skelton Grange has been announced. The 19 August 2026 announced observation is kept.
